tagline: Project management for distributed product teams
bio: Helix HQ is a bootstrapped SaaS company founded in 2021 that helps distributed product teams manage sprints, roadmaps, and stakeholder updates in one place. The product serves 1,200 paying customers across 34 countries, with a focus on teams of 5–50 people. 100% bootstrapped, profitable since month 18.
executive_summary: Helix HQ has crossed $3.2M ARR at 85% gross margin and is growing 8% MoM. The company operates without venture backing and maintains 24 months of runway. This report covers product-led growth optimization, expansion revenue opportunities, competitive positioning against Jira and Linear, and the technical scalability roadmap needed to serve teams of 50–500.

key_assumptions: PLG free-to-paid conversion improves from 4.1% to 6% by Q4
Enterprise tier (100+ seat) launched Q3 at $12/seat/month
No paid acquisition — organic + word-of-mouth only

risk_items.risk: Linear continues to take mid-market share with superior DX and faster velocity
risk_items.mitigation: Differentiate on stakeholder-facing features (roadmap sharing, exec dashboards) that Linear deliberately avoids

risk_items.risk: Database read latency degrades beyond 200ms at 50k+ concurrent workspaces
risk_items.mitigation: Implement read replicas and connection pooling before 40k workspace threshold

risk_items.risk: Bus factor: 2 engineers own the core data pipeline
risk_items.mitigation: Documentation sprint Q2; pair rotation policy; hire 1 senior backend engineer Q3

roadmap_items.milestone: Stakeholder view — read-only roadmap sharing with external stakeholders
Enterprise tier launch with SSO (SAML), audit log, and admin controls
AI sprint summarization — auto-generate sprint retrospectives

competitive_data.strength: Dominant market share; deep CI/CD integrations; enterprise procurement relationships
competitive_data.weakness: Notoriously complex UX; expensive at scale; slow velocity of improvement
competitive_data.positioning: Enterprise default — win by simplicity and onboarding speed

competitive_data.strength: Best-in-class developer experience; extremely fast UI; strong brand among engineers
competitive_data.weakness: No stakeholder-facing features; no roadmap sharing; minimal reporting
competitive_data.positioning: Developer-first — differentiate on product + stakeholder layer

competitive_data.strength: All-in-one positioning; massive existing user base
competitive_data.weakness: Weak at structured project tracking; no sprint velocity metrics
competitive_data.positioning: All-in-one — win on dedicated PM features

ai_narratives.growth_analysis: Helix HQ's 8.2% MoM growth is durable because it is driven almost entirely by organic channels: word-of-mouth from satisfied users and SEO. The PLG funnel is the primary lever to pull — moving free-to-paid conversion from 4.1% to 6% would add $68k MRR at current free tier volume without any increase in acquisition spend. The enterprise tier launch in Q3 represents the first meaningful expansion revenue motion; the target of $12/seat/month is below Linear's $8/member/month but above Jira's bundled pricing at scale.
ai_narratives.competitive_positioning: Helix HQ's strongest moat is not features but onboarding velocity. New teams are live in under 10 minutes; Jira migrations typically take 2–8 weeks. This time-to-value advantage should be the centerpiece of the Q3 growth campaign. The risk is that Linear closes the stakeholder feature gap — monitoring Linear's public roadmap is a required activity for the product team.

audience_data.primary_persona: Head of Product at 20–100 person software company
